questionText: Friedmann equations:
options: They are a set of equations in physical cosmology that govern the expansion of space in homogeneous and isotropic models of the universe within the context of general relativity.

They were first derived by Alexander Friedmann in 1922 from Einstein's field equations of gravitation. According to the equations, the Universe isn't static. It either expands or contracts depending on the rate of expansion and the contents of the Universe.
The Friedmann equation derived from Newtonian mechanics accounts only for the gravity contribution to energy and neglects the pressure contribution to the total energy.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Friedmann' as 'Fried-Man' who cooked up the recipe for an expanding universe using Einstein's ingredients.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Chandrasekhar limit:
options: The Chandrasekhar limit is the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star.
The Chandrasekhar value for a white dwarf star is generally considered to be 1.4 solar masses.
Before reaching a white dwarf state, stars first lose mass by shedding their outer layers.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember '1.4' as the 'Chandrasekhar Ceiling'—the maximum weight a white dwarf can hold before collapsing.

questionText: Gravitational lensing occurs when:
options: A massive celestial body causes a sufficient curvature of spacetime for the path of light around it to be visibly bent.
The body causing the light to curve is called a gravitational lens.
Gravitational lensing probes the distribution of matter in galaxies and clusters of galaxies.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of a 'Lens' as a 'Bend' in the 'Space-time' fabric caused by a 'Massive' object.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Tidal Disruption Events (TDE):
options: TDE occur when a star passes too close to a compact object, such as a supermassive black hole.
When a black hole swallows approaching stars, it shreds them into strands like spaghetti.
A jet of light particles is emitted, appearing as an intensely bright flash of light due to Doppler boosting.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'TDE' as 'Tidal Destruction Ejection': Tidal forces destroy the star, and the black hole ejects a bright light.

questionText: Nanotechnology can be used for:
options: Multimodal imaging and synergistic phototherapy to destroy cancer cells.
Water purification using nanoscopic materials such as carbon nanotubes and alumina fibers.
Electrospinning to produce a novel fabric that offers high-performance protection against electromagnetic interference.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'NANO' as 'N-ew A-pplications N-early O-mnipresent'—covering health, water, and tech.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Nanorobotics:
options: It is a mechanical or electromechanical device that can design and build nanorobots ranging in size from 0.1 to 10 micrometres.
The first useful applications of nanomachines may be in nanomedicines.
Earlier nanites have been tested for water purification purposes.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think 'NANO': Nanomedicine, Applications in water, Nanites, and Operations at micro-scale.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Liquid nano urea:
options: It is sprayed directly on the leaves and gets absorbed by the plant.
Liquid nano urea has a shelf life of a year and is not likely to undergo ‘caking’.
The Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative Limited (IFFCO) has developed and patented nano urea liquid technology.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'L-I-F-E': Leaves (foliar), IFFCO (developer), Fertilizer (nano), Extended shelf-life.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Quasars:
options: Quasars are a subclass of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), extremely luminous galactic cores.
They are powered by a supermassive black hole feeding on humongous quantities of gas.
They are amongst the most luminous objects in the known Universe.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of a Q-U-A-S-A-R as a 'QUickly Accreting Supermassive Active Region'.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Rogue planets:
options: Rogue planets are cosmic objects that have masses similar to the planets in the Solar System but do not orbit a star.
Astronomers have discovered at least 70 new rogue planets in the Milky Way galaxy.
Rogue planets are directly detectable by sensitive cameras on large telescopes in the few million years after their formation.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Rogue' as 'Roaming'—planets that roam the galaxy alone without a stellar parent.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and Microreactors:
options: SMRs have a power capacity of up to 300 MW(e) per unit.
SMRs have reduced fuel requirements compared to conventional plants.
Microreactors are 100 to 1,000 times smaller than conventional nuclear reactors.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: SMRs are 'Small, Modular, and Rapid'—300 MW is the magic limit for their modular design.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding radioactive materials:
options: Polonium-210 (Po-210) is a radioactive material that occurs naturally in the Earth’s crust.
Carbon-14 is the longest-lived radioactive isotope of carbon.
Americium-241 is the most common form of Americium.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'PAC': Polonium (naturally occurring), Americium (common smoke detector isotope), Carbon-14 (long-lived dating tool).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Thorium:
options: Thorium is a naturally occurring radioactive metal found at trace levels in soil, rocks, water, plants and animals.
Thorium alone cannot be directly used as nuclear fuel in a reactor.
Monazite resources are found in Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.
All of the above
concepts: Distribution of mineral resources in India
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'T-M-O' for Thorium: Thorium is fertile (not fissile), Monazite is the source, and Odisha/coastal states are the hubs.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding nuclear reactors:
options: Nuclear reactors use uranium fuel rods containing pellets of fissionable material to create energy through fission.
Criticality is the normal operating condition of a nuclear reactor, in which nuclear fuel sustains a fission chain reaction.
A reactor achieves criticality when each fission releases a sufficient number of neutrons to sustain an ongoing series of nuclear reactions.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'C-C-S': Criticality means Chain-reaction Sustained.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Rosalind Franklin rover:
options: The Rosalind Franklin is a planned robotic Mars rover, part of the international ExoMars programme.
ExoMars is a joint endeavour between the European Space Agency (ESA) and Russia's Roscosmos agency.
The rover’s intended landing site is a vast plain called Oxia Planum.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'REO': Rosalind (rover), ExoMars (program), Oxia (landing site).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs):
options: CMEs are large expulsions of plasma and magnetic fields from the Sun’s corona.
CMEs are capable of disrupting radio waves which can result in a radio blackout.
Solar storms have no direct impact on humans on Earth’s surface.
All of the above
concepts: Impact of Solar Flares on Earth's Atmosphere
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'CME' as 'Corona's Magnetic Ejection'—it's a solar sneeze that disrupts our radio breeze.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST):
options: JWST is the world’s premier space science observatory developed by NASA.
It primarily studies the universe in the infrared.
It sits at the Earth-Sun L2 Lagrange Point at a distance of 1.5 million km from Earth.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'JWST' as 'Just Watch Space Through' infrared at L2.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Dark matter:
options: Dark matter makes up around 85 per cent of the matter in the known universe.
Dark matter is completely invisible as it doesn't interact with light.
Particles that make up Dark matter do not have a charge.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'D-I-N': Dark matter is Invisible, Non-interacting with light, and has no charge.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding launch vehicles:
options: PSLV is designed mainly to deliver the “earth-observation” or “remote-sensing” satellites.
GSLV is designed mainly to deliver the satellites to the highly elliptical Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
GSLV Mk-III is configured as a three-stage vehicle with two solid strap-on motors.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'P-E-R' (PSLV-Earth-Remote) and 'G-G-T' (GSLV-Geosynchronous-Transfer) to distinguish their primary missions.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding space stations:
options: A space station is a spacecraft capable of supporting crew members, designed to remain in space for an extended period of time.
Tiangong space station is China's new permanent space station.
The Tiangong space station is being independently built by China.
All of the above
sub_topic: International Space Stations and Space Exploration
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Tiangong' as 'Tian-Gone' to space, China's solo home in the sky.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding exoplanets:
options: An exoplanet is any planet beyond our solar system.
Exoplanets are composed of a variety of elements, and some exoplanets have been found to have similar compositions to the planets in our solar system.
Exoplanets come in a wide range of sizes, from small rocky planets similar to Earth to large gas giants similar to Jupiter.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of EXO as 'Extra-Solar'—anything outside our home solar system is an exoplanet.

questionText: What is the correct sequence of stellar evolution for an average star?
options: Stellar Nebula, Red Giant, Planetary Nebula and White Dwarf.
Stellar Nebula, Planetary Nebula, Red Giant and White Dwarf.
Stellar Nebula, White Dwarf, Red Giant and Planetary Nebula.
Stellar Nebula, Red Giant, White Dwarf and Planetary Nebula.
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'SN-RG-PN-WD': Super Novae Rarely Get Past New Worlds Daily.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Lucy Mission:
options: It was launched by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) in 2021.
It is the first spacecraft launched to explore the Trojan asteroids.
The mission is named after the fossilised skeleton of an early human ancestor.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Lucy' as the 'Human Ancestor' who went on a 'Trojan Horse' ride through space to visit the asteroids.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Neutron Stars:
options: A Neutron Star is the collapsed core of a massive Supergiant Star.
Neutron stars are incredibly dense - similar to the density of an atomic nucleus.
Neutron star collisions are one of the universe’s main sources of heavy elements like gold and uranium.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of a Neutron star as a 'Cosmic Gold Mine'—it is a dense core that crashes to create heavy metals.

questionText: The Giant-Impact theory explains:
options: The formation of the Moon.
The formation of the Sun.
The formation of the Earth.
The formation of the Milky Way.
sub_topic: Origin and Evolution of the Earth and Moon
mnemonic_hint: Think of the Moon as a 'Giant' piece of Earth that broke off during a massive 'Impact'.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR):
options: NISAR is a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) observatory jointly developed by NASA and ISRO.
It consists of both L-band and S-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) instruments.
NISAR will be the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies to measure changes in our planet’s surface.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'NISAR' as 'NASA-ISRO SAR'—where the 'L' and 'S' in the name stand for the L-band and S-band radars it carries.

questionText: Consider the following pairs of Earth orbits and their applications:
options: Low Earth Orbit (LEO): Communication and remote sensing satellite systems.
Geosynchronous Orbit (GSO): Consistent position over a single longitude.
Geostationary Orbit (GEO): Telecommunications and Earth observation.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: LEO is Low (close/fast), GSO is Geosynchronous (syncs with Earth's rotation), and GEO is Geostationary (fixed point in the sky).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding black holes:
options: A 'stationary limit' is a surface around the outside of a rotating black hole.
The 'event horizon' is a surface that exists closer to the black hole.
The ergosphere lies just outside the event horizon of a rotating black hole.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'S-E-E': Stationary limit is outer, Ergosphere is middle, Event horizon is inner.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Indian satellites:
options: ‘EDUSAT’ is India’s first thematic satellite dedicated exclusively to educational services.
The Indian National Satellite System (INSAT/GSAT) is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
INSAT has been a major catalyst for the expansion of television coverage in India.
All of the above
sub_topic: Indian Space Programme and Satellite Systems
concepts: Role of Space Technology in Mass Media
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'E-I-I': EDUSAT for Education, INSAT for Infrastructure (Communication), and INSAT for Information (TV coverage).

questionText: Consider the following international space treaties:
options: Outer Space Treaty, 1967
Rescue Agreement of 1968
Liability Convention of 1972
All of the above
concepts: International Legal Frameworks for Outer Space
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'ORL' for the chronological order: Outer Space (1967), Rescue (1968), Liability (1972).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ):
options: It is a next-generation dark matter experiment.
It is located at the Sanford Underground Research Facility.
It utilises a two-phase time projection chamber (TPC), containing seven active tonnes of liquid xenon.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'LZ-Xenon-Deep': LZ is the experiment, Xenon is the medium, and it is buried Deep underground.

questionText: Consider the following Indian satellites and their applications in Disaster Management:
options: Radar Imaging Satellite-2B (RISAT-2B)
Earth Observation Satellite-3 (EOS-3)
Indian National Satellite-3D Repeat (INSAT-3DR)
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'R-E-I' for Disaster: Radar (RISAT) for imaging, Earth (EOS) for observation, and INSAT for weather monitoring.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding constellations:
options: Constellations are groupings of stars that were imagined to form conspicuous configurations of objects or creatures in the sky.
Stars and constellations stay in approximately the same spot for many years.
Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Draco, Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are some of the constellations that can be seen all year long in the northern hemisphere.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'C-C-D-U-U' for the northern sky: Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Draco, Ursa Major, and Ursa Minor.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Multi-Angle Imager for Aerosols (MAIA) mission:
options: MAIA is a joint mission between NASA and the Italian Space Agency ASI.
It will be able to collect measurements of sunlight reflecting off airborne particles.
The mission will investigate the health impacts of air pollution in the world’s most populated cities.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: MAIA: Monitoring Aerosols, Investigating Air-health (NASA + Italian Agency).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Nuclear Fission and Nuclear Fusion:
options: Nuclear Fission occurs when a neutron strikes a larger atom, forcing it to excite and split into two smaller atoms.
The source of energy of the sun is nuclear fusion.
Nuclear fission power plants have the disadvantage of generating unstable nuclei which remain radioactive for millions of years.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Fission is 'Division' (splitting atoms), Fusion is 'Union' (combining atoms to make the Sun shine).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Cordy Gold Nanoparticles (Cor-AuNPs):
options: Cor-AuNPs are derived from the synthesis of the extracts of Cordyceps militaris and gold salts.
These nanoparticles add bioactive components to the synthesis of gold nanoparticles for better penetration.
These biosynthesized nanogold particles can be used in the development of therapeutic drugs.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think 'C-G-T': Cordyceps + Gold = Therapeutic potential.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding nuclear reactors:
options: Pressurised-Water Reactor (PWR) utilises ordinary water as both coolant and moderator.
Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) generally uses natural uranium oxide as fuel.
Fast Breeder Reactor (FBR) is a type of nuclear reactor that produces more nuclear fuels than it consumes.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'PHWR-Natural' (PHWR uses natural uranium) and 'FBR-Breeds' (FBR creates more fuel than it uses).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding a Total Solar Eclipse:
options: A Total Solar Eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, completely blocking the face of the Sun.
The solar corona becomes visible during totality.
The Diamond Ring Effect is created by the single jewel of light from the Sun.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'S-M-E' (Sun-Moon-Earth) for the alignment and 'Corona-Diamond' for the visual highlights of a total eclipse.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Dark Sky Reserve:
options: A Dark Sky Reserve is public or private land with a distinguished nocturnal environment and starry nights that have been developed responsibly to prevent light pollution.
The Department of Science and Technology will set up India’s first Dark Sky Reserve at Ladakh’s Hanle.
The primary objective of the proposed Dark Sky Reserve is to promote astronomy tourism in a sustainable and environment-friendly manner.
All of the above
sub_topic: Dark Sky Reserves and Light Pollution
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'HALO': Hanle, Astronomy, Ladakh, Observatory—the first Dark Sky Reserve.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Nanomicelles:
options: Nanomicelles are ultramicroscopic structures used in the treatment of diseases.
They have a hydrophilic outer shell and a hydrophobic exterior.
Nanomicelles are an emerging platform in targeted therapy and are being used for cancer treatment.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of a 'Nano-Micelle' as a 'Hydro-Phobic-Philic' sandwich: water-loving outside, oil-loving inside, carrying medicine to the target.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding nanotechnology applications in agriculture:
options: Crop production through the use of nano herbicides/nano pesticides and nanomaterials to control the viral and fungal diseases of plants.
It helps in precision farming.
The degradation of the nanomaterials and/or nanocomposites under environmental conditions may cause nanotoxicity.
All of the above
concepts: Applications of Nanotechnology in Crop Protection
mnemonic_hint: Think 'P-E-D': Precision farming, Environmental toxicity, and Disease control are the three pillars of Nano-Agri.

questionText: Nanoflakes of a material called hematene extracted from iron ore have been found capable of:
options: Withstanding and acting as shields from high laser intensities.
Protecting sensitive optical equipment from light-induced damage.
Being ferromagnetic like a common magnet.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Hematene' as a 'Heavy-duty' shield: it blocks lasers, protects optics, and holds magnetic power.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Artemis Accords:
options: The Artemis Accords are a set of non-legally binding principles to guide sustainable civil space exploration.
NASA established the Artemis Accords in 2020 together with seven other founding member nations.
The Republic of India became the 27th nation to sign the Artemis Accords.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'ARTEMIS' as 'A-R-T-E-M-I-S': All-countries, Rules-non-binding, Twenty-seven-members, Exploration-Moon, International-Space-cooperation.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Standard Model of Particle Physics:
options: The Standard Model of Particle Physics is scientists’ current best theory to describe the most basic building blocks of the universe.
The Standard Model explains three of the four fundamental forces that govern the universe: electromagnetism, the strong nuclear force, and the weak force.
It explains how the entire Universe is built from just twelve matter particles called fermions.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'SEW' for the forces: Strong, Electromagnetism, and Weak (Gravity is the odd one out).

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Lagrange points:
options: Lagrange points are positions in space where objects sent there tend to stay put.
There are five special points where a small mass can orbit in a constant pattern with two larger masses.
Of the five Lagrange points, three are unstable and two are stable.
All of the above
concepts: Centrifugal force in rotating reference frames
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'L1-L5' as 'L1-L3 are unstable (like a balancing act) and L4-L5 are stable (like a cozy nest) where objects stay put.'

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Aditya L1:
options: Aditya L1 shall be the first space based Indian mission to study the Sun.
Using the special vantage point L1, four payloads directly view the Sun and the remaining three payloads carry out in-situ studies.
A satellite placed in the halo orbit around the L1 point has the major advantage of continuously viewing the Sun without any occultation/eclipses.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'L1-SUN': L1 is the Location, 1st mission, 4 payloads view, 3 in-situ, No-occultation.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding JT-60SA:
options: JT-60SA is a joint initiative between the European Union and Japan.
It comprises a doughnut-shaped “tokamak” vessel set to contain the swirling plasma.
JT-60SA is a forerunner for the under-construction International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER).
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'JT' as 'Joint Team' (Japan-EU) working on a 'Tokamak' to prepare for the 'ITER' future.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding gravitational waves:
options: Gravitational waves originate from the most violent and energetic events in the cosmos.
LIGO, a laser interferometer tool, is designed to detect gravitational waves.
LIGO-India will be an addition to the already existing facilities of this type.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'LIGO' as 'Light Interferes, Gravity Oscillates' to recall its detection mechanism.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding gravitational waves:
options: They are ripples in the fabric of spacetime caused by the most energetic events in the cosmos.
Higher-frequency gravitational waves come from smaller pairs of black holes zipping around each other rapidly.
India’s Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT, Pune) played a vital role in providing evidence for low-frequency gravitational waves.
All of the above
sub_topic: Gravitational Waves and Pulsar Timing Arrays
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'GMRT' as the 'Gravity-Meter Radio Telescope' that listens to the cosmic hum of spacetime ripples.

questionText: ISRO's mission objectives for the Chandrayaan-3 mission are:
options: Engineering and implementing a lander to land safely and softly on the surface of the Moon.
Observing and demonstrating the rover's driving capabilities on the Moon.
Conducting and observing experiments on the materials available on the lunar surface.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'L-D-E': Land safely, Drive the rover, Experiment on lunar soil.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Gaganyaan program:
options: The Government of India has approved two unmanned missions and one manned mission as part of the Gaganyaan program.
A modified version of ISRO’s most-reliable rocket, LVM3, is the launching vehicle of the Gaganyaan Mission.
India and France joined forces for India’s ambitious human spaceflight initiative named Gaganyaan.
All of the above
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'G-L-F': Gaganyaan uses LVM3 and partners with France (CNES).
